story.head: Kucherov’s favorite opponent
paras: The Lightning (12-4-2) beat Buffalo 8-3 last night, while the Blue Jackets (7-9-0) lost 4-1 to Florida on Tuesday. Going in, the Bolts are second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets last in the Metropolitan (29th).

The Lightning’s record (.722) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.667), largely thanks to their finishing. The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.438) says: their chances are worth about .492.
This season, the Blue Jackets have been outscored 51-39, but only 29-26 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 13-7.

The Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (4th), but don't block many shots (29th). Tampa Bay has scored 3.94 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Blue Jackets forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), get their defensemen shooting (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (29th). Columbus has scored 2.44 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league.

Nikita Kucherov (8 G / 18 A / 26 P in 18 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Columbus. Brandon Hagel (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 16 GP) is next in line.
Dennis Hildeby (3-0-1 / .880 SV% in 4 GS) is expected to start for Tampa Bay, and Jet Greaves (2-6-0 / .879 SV% in 8 GS) for Columbus.
At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Hagel, Cirelli and Kucherov.
